# besttraveler

> besttraveler (https://besttraveler.ge) is a Georgian travel company that runs group tours from Georgia (Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Yerevan airports, or by minibus from Tbilisi) to 26 countries, and one-day tours around Georgia. Tour organiser: Natali Iashvili. Contact: phone/WhatsApp +995 579 57 56 36, email info@besttraveler.ge. The site is in Georgian (default), English (/en/) and Russian (/ru/).

Booking: a deposit holds a place; the rest is paid 15 days before the tour; money is not returned if the traveller cancels for their own reasons. Payment by bank transfer. Prices of flight tours depend on air fares and can change.


# Booking terms

## Booking and deposit

You hold a place on a tour with a deposit. The deposit amount is shown on each tour page. To confirm a place, contact us by phone or WhatsApp.

## Paying the rest

The rest of the price (minus the deposit) is paid 15 days before the tour starts. Some long-haul tours (for example China) have a different deadline — it is shown on the tour page.

Payment is by bank transfer to our Bank of Georgia or TBC Bank account. We send the account details when you book.

## Price

Flight tour prices are based on current air fares. Fares rise as the departure gets closer, so the price can change — book early and confirm the price before you pay.

## Refunds

- If you cannot travel for your own reasons, the money you paid is not returned.
- The money is not returned if you cannot cross the border because your passport has expired, is not valid long enough, or for another violation.
- On a one-day tour the money is not returned if you cancel in the last two days.

## Documents

- To cross the border you need an international passport valid for at least 6 months.
- For tours to Armenia and Turkey you can travel with a passport or a Georgian ID card.
- Minors need a birth certificate, notarised consent from the parents and an international passport.
- Whether a visa is needed, and its fee, is shown on each tour page (under “Not included”).

## Airlines and weather

- The tour company is not responsible for problems caused by the airline (delays, cancellations, luggage).
- One-day tours run in any weather. A tour is postponed only if there is a problem with the road.


# FAQ

**How do I book a tour?** Call or message us on WhatsApp at +995 579 57 56 36. We confirm a free place and the price, then you hold the place with a deposit. The rest is paid 15 days before the tour.

**How do I pay?** By bank transfer to our Bank of Georgia or TBC Bank account. We send the account details when you book.

**Are flights included in the price?** On most flight tours the return flight is included. Each tour page lists exactly what is and is not included.

**Why can the price change?** Flight tour prices are based on current air fares. Fares go up as the trip gets closer, so it is best to book early.

**Which documents do I need?** To cross the border you need an international passport valid for at least 6 months. For tours to Armenia and Turkey a Georgian ID card is also accepted. Children need a birth certificate, notarised consent from the parents and a passport.

**Where do the day tours start?** Day tours start in Tbilisi and go by minibus. The meeting point is usually the upper exit of Didube metro station.

**Do I get my money back if I cannot go?** If you cannot travel for your own reasons, the money you paid is not returned. See the booking terms for details.

**Day 4:** Transfer to the airport; Flight to Kutaisi at 08:35; Arrival in Kutaisi at 12:10

A 6-day tour of Turkey by comfortable bus. We never travel overnight: every night is spent in a hotel.

**Day 1:** 06:00 departure from Tbilisi (via Sarpi) to Amasya; Hotel check-in, free time, evening walk in the city
**Day 2:** Amasya city; Rock tombs of the Pontic kings; Amasya Castle; Avanos, an ancient town of craftsmen; Monks Valley, with formations of volcanic origin; Hotel check-in
**Day 3:** Hot-air balloon flight (optional), or photos with the balloons in the background; Goreme Open-Air Museum (10th-15th century churches); Silver shop (souvenir market), camel ride; Tokali Church, with a unique fresco that is the prototype of the icon 'Thou Art the Vine'; Uchisar Castle; Pigeon Valley; Turkish Night (optional, 30 EUR)
**Day 4:** Pasabag (Queens' Gardens): the cell of St Simeon Stylites and multi-headed fairy chimneys; the place where vines were first grown in Anatolia; Zelve, the Valley of the Monks; House of St George's mother (where, by tradition, St George lived); St Nino's village (Ortahisar Castle); Saruhan Caravanserai (1249); Pancarlik Church, one of the longest church interiors in the world
**Day 5:** Kayseri Castle, built in antiquity; Kayseri bazaar (optional); Gumusler Monastery; Ordu, hotel check-in; Ordu cable car (optional), with panoramic views of the city, the Black Sea and Boztepe hill
**Day 6:** Trabzon; Little Hagia Sophia; Shopping centre (optional); Return to Tbilisi

Included:
- Travel by comfortable bus (air conditioning, internet in Turkey)
- 4-5 star hotels in Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu
- Breakfasts and dinners
- Qualified Georgian-speaking guide and tour organiser

Not included:
- Local fees (300 GEL)
- Ordu cable car (optional)

Optional extras:
- Hot-air balloon flight: 200-250 EUR (optional)
- Turkish Night: 30 EUR (optional)

Notes:
- Alcohol and smoking are not allowed on the bus.

## Nile Cruise: Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel, Hurghada and El Gouna

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/nile-cruise-luxor-aswan-hurghada/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Egypt
- Duration: 8 days
- Price: 4,500 GEL per person (deposit 1,500 GEL)
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: 8–15 Nov 2026, 6–13 Dec 2026, 24–31 Jan 2027, 21–28 Feb 2027, 21–28 Mar 2027, 18–25 Apr 2027, 23–30 May 2027

An 8-day tour of Egypt with a Georgian-speaking tour leader from Tbilisi. It includes St Anthony's Monastery, 4 nights on a 5-star Nile cruise ship, the temples of Luxor and Aswan, and El Gouna.

**Day 1:** Flight from Tbilisi airport at 04:25; Arrival in Hurghada at 09:30; St Anthony's Monastery — the world's oldest working Christian monastery. St Anthony the Great (251–356) lived as a hermit and died in a cave in the cliff above it; Church of St Anthony with very old frescoes; Church of St Paul of Thebes; Old library and manuscripts; Monks' cells
**Day 2:** Luxor; Karnak Temple — one of the grandest monuments of ancient Egypt (20th century BC – 1st century AD); Temple of Hatshepsut — a unique monument of ancient Egyptian architecture (15th century BC); Valley of the Kings — one of the most important necropolises of ancient Egypt (16th–11th centuries BC)
**Day 3:** Hot-air balloon flight (optional, extra cost); Luxor Temple — one of the most elegant and historically important temples of ancient Egypt (14th century BC); Free time on the ship
**Day 4:** Temple of Edfu — one of the best-preserved temples of ancient Egypt, dedicated to the god Horus (237–57 BC); Temple of Kom Ombo — unique because it is dedicated to two gods at once (2nd–1st centuries BC)
**Day 5:** Abu Simbel (optional, 200 USD) — two temples cut into the rock by Ramesses II in the 13th century BC: the Great Temple (Ramesses II) and the Small Temple (Nefertari); Philae Temple — one of the best-known temples in Egypt, dedicated to the goddess Isis; Nubian village (optional, 50 USD) — a small traditional village on the Nile, known for its colourful houses, art and hospitality
**Day 6:** Optional (250 USD): Wadi es-Sebua — an ancient Egyptian temple complex, mostly from the New Kingdom (13th century BC); Optional: Temple of Derr — a small but historically important temple built under Ramesses II (13th century BC); Travel to Hurghada
**Day 7:** El Gouna — a modern resort on the Red Sea coast
**Day 8:** Flight to Tbilisi at 03:20; Arrival at 15:50

Included:
- Round-trip flight Tbilisi–Istanbul–Hurghada
- 20 kg baggage
- Hotels with meals
- 5-star cruise ship (4 nights) with meals
- Transfers
- Travel insurance
- Local guide
- Georgian-speaking tour leader from Tbilisi
- Group excursions
- Entrance fees to historic sites (except optional excursions)

Not included:
- Visa fee (25 USD)
- Optional excursions

Optional extras:
- Abu Simbel — 200 USD (optional)
- Wadi es-Sebua and the Temple of Derr — 250 USD (optional)
- Nubian village — 50 USD (optional)
- Hot-air balloon flight — 90 USD (optional)

**Day 6:** Optional (100 USD): jeep tour to the Red Canyon, Dahab, Mount Sinai and St Catherine's Monastery — the place where, by tradition, Moses received the Ten Commandments, and the Burning Bush; Or optional (50 USD): jeep tour to the Red and White Canyons, quad tour and camel ride
**Day 7:** Optional glass-bottom boat trip on the Red Sea to see sea life (30 USD)

An 8-day tour of Upper and Lower Normandy, Brittany and the Loire region: seaside towns, medieval fortresses and famous châteaux.

**Day 3:** Rouen: the Gothic Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Gros-Horloge astronomical clock and the Old Market Square; Domaine du Champ de Bataille, 17th century (gardens 15 EUR, château and gardens 27 EUR); Fougères — a historic town in Brittany; Château de Fougères, with 13 towers (10 EUR)
**Day 4:** Mont-Saint-Michel — a village and abbey on a rocky island, a UNESCO site; Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey (20 EUR); Saint-Malo — a Brittany seaside town with a walled old town; Dinan — a medieval town in the Rance valley; Château de Goulaine near Nantes
**Day 5:** La Rochelle — an Atlantic port town with an old harbour; Fort Boyard — a sea fort in the Atlantic near La Rochelle; Chinon — a Loire Valley town with a royal fortress
**Day 6:** Château d’Ussé — white towers and terraced gardens (15 EUR); Amboise — a historic town on the Loire; Château de Chenonceau — the château built like a bridge over the river Cher (18 EUR)
**Day 7:** Château de Chambord — the largest Renaissance château of the Loire Valley (17 EUR); Château de Fontainebleau — a royal palace, a UNESCO site (14 EUR)
**Day 8:** Château de Chantilly — a château on the water with gardens and stables (18 EUR)

## 5 Countries in One Tour by Car: France, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/alps-switzerland-5-countries-tour/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Switzerland, France, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein
- Duration: 8 days / 7 nights
- Price: 4,500 GEL per person (deposit 1,000 GEL)
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: 14–21 Jun 2027, 5–12 Jul 2027, 2–9 Aug 2027, 6–13 Sep 2027

A group tour by car through France, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria and Germany. The tour starts and ends in Geneva.

**Day 1:** Flight from Tbilisi at 13:45; Arrival at Geneva airport at 16:30; Geneva
**Day 2:** Annecy (France) — a town often called 'the Venice of the Alps'; Yvoire — a medieval village on the French shore of Lake Geneva; Château de Chillon; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 3:** Gruyères — a medieval Swiss town known for its Gruyère cheese, castle and Alpine views; Château de Gruyères (15 EUR); Jaun Waterfall (Wasserfall von Jaun); Lauterbrunnen — one of Switzerland's most beautiful valleys, the 'valley of 72 waterfalls'; Gimmelwald — an Alpine village above the Lauterbrunnen valley, at about 1,367 m (by cable car); Mürren — an Alpine village above the valley, at about 1,638 m (Gimmelwald–Mürren cable car 35 EUR); Grindelwald — one of Switzerland's best-known Alpine resorts; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 4:** Lucerne (Switzerland) — known for its covered wooden bridge built in 1333, with 17th-century paintings inside; Einsiedeln Abbey — a Benedictine abbey dating back to the 10th century; Balzers — a small town in Liechtenstein; Vaduz — the capital of the Principality of Liechtenstein; Lech am Arlberg — a well-known Alpine resort in Austria; Hotel (Austria)
**Day 5:** Linderhof Palace (Germany) — the only one of King Ludwig II of Bavaria's three palaces that he saw completed; Ettal Abbey (Kloster Ettal) — a Benedictine monastery in the Bavarian Alps; Oberammergau — a Bavarian village known for its painted houses, woodcarving and the Passion Play; Hotel (Germany)
**Day 6:** Neuschwanstein (Germany) — one of the most famous castles in the world, built for Ludwig II from 1869; Meersburg — a historic town on Lake Constance (Bodensee); Rhine Falls (Rheinfall), Switzerland; Baden (Switzerland) — a small historic spa town; Basel — a city in north-western Switzerland; Thun (Switzerland) — a town on Lake Thun and the Aare river, known for its medieval castle and old town; Hotel (Switzerland)
**Day 7:** Bern — the Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; Palais de Rumine, Lausanne; Geneva
**Day 8:** Transfer to the airport; Flight to Tbilisi at 06:30

Included:
- Return flights Tbilisi–Geneva–Tbilisi
- Hand luggage 10 kg (40x30x20 cm)
- Transport for the whole tour, airport to airport
- Hotels with breakfast
- Tour escort
- Photography
- Travel insurance

Not included:

**Day 13:** Giresun; Check in at the hotel, free time

- Nights: Tokat, Eskişehir (2), Izmir, Çeşme (2), Akyaka, Marmaris (2), Göcek, Side, Göreme, Giresun

## India Group Tour: Rajasthan, Delhi, Jaisalmer and Udaipur

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/india-rajasthan-group-tour/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: India
- Duration: 9 days / 8 nights
- Price: 4,800 GEL per person
- Departure: From Tbilisi airport
- Dates: on request

A 9-day / 8-night group tour of India: Delhi and the cities of Rajasthan, including Mandawa, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Ranakpur, Udaipur and Pushkar. Departure from Tbilisi on 25 October at 23:45.

**Day 1: Tbilisi to Delhi and Mandawa:** Flight from Tbilisi on 25 October at 23:45, arrival in Delhi on 26 October at 07:05; Transfer to the hotel; after breakfast, drive to Mandawa; Mandawa havelis, houses once owned by wealthy merchants; Breakfast, dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 2: Mandawa to Bikaner:** Binsidhar Newatia Haveli, known for its bright, lively paintings; Gulab Rai Ladia Haveli, Goenka Double Haveli, Murmuria Haveli, Jhunjhunwala Haveli; Drive to Bikaner: Junagarh Fort, decorated with gold leaf, glass, mirror work and Dutch tiles; Breakfast, dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 3: Bikaner to Jaisalmer:** Jaisalmer Fort, standing about 100 metres high; Havelis with carved facades and windows; Salim Singh Haveli (17th century), known for its peacock carvings; Nathumal Haveli (1885) and Patwon Haveli (1805); Dinner and overnight at the hotel
**Day 4: Jaisalmer to Jodhpur:** Drive to Jodhpur, hotel check-in and free time; Mehrangarh Fort on a 125-metre hill, one of the most impressive buildings in Rajasthan; Jaswant Thada, a white marble memorial (1899) to Maharaja Jaswant Singh II; Evening: the Clock Tower and Sardar Bazaar, with textiles, antiques, silverware and handicrafts; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 5: Jodhpur to Udaipur via Ranakpur:** Ranakpur temples (15th century), famous for their intricate architecture; Arrival in Udaipur, transfer to the hotel; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 6: Udaipur, the City of Lakes:** City Palace, the former home of the Mewar rulers, now mostly a museum overlooking Lake Pichola; Jagdish Mandir; Sahelion ki Bari; Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal; Evening boat ride on Lake Pichola; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 7: Udaipur to Pushkar:** Brahma Temple and the ghats; Pushkar, a town on the shore of Pushkar Lake; Breakfast and overnight at the hotel
**Day 8: Pushkar to Delhi:** After breakfast, drive to Delhi; Free time
**Day 9: Delhi to Tbilisi:** Qutub Minar; India Gate; President's House and Parliament; Bangla Sahib; Agrasen ki Baoli, a historic stepwell 60 m long and 15 m wide; Dinner at Lazeez restaurant, then transfer to the international airport

Included:
- Return flights Tbilisi-Delhi-Tbilisi
- 30 kg baggage
- 4-5 star hotels
- Two meals a day (breakfast and dinner)
- Internal transfers
- Travel insurance
- Local guide
- Georgian-speaking tour escort from Tbilisi
- Group excursions
- Boat ride on Lake Pichola
- Entrance fees to architectural sites
- All taxes and fees

## Sicily and Southern Italy — 8-Day Tour from Yerevan

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/tours/sicily-southern-italy-tour/

- Type: By plane
- Countries: Italy

The tour starts with a flight from Yerevan to Italy, follows the coast of southern Italy and crosses to Sicily by ferry. On the island we visit Palermo, Monreale, Agrigento, the baroque towns and Catania.

**Day 1:** Flight from Yerevan at 12:05; Arrival in Naples at 14:15; Salerno, one of the most beautiful towns in southern Italy
**Day 2:** Paola; Sanctuary of St Francis of Paola, an important pilgrimage site in southern Italy where St Francis of Paola rests; Chiesetta di Piedigrotta, a church carved entirely into a seaside rock, with dozens of statues also carved from the rock; Villa San Giovanni; Ferry crossing to Sicily; Messina, Sicily's third-largest city and the main port gateway from mainland Italy
**Day 3:** Cefalù, one of the most beautiful seaside towns in Sicily; Palermo, the capital and largest city of Sicily
**Day 4:** Monreale, a historic hillside town known for its Norman cathedral, built in 1174–1189 by order of King William II; a UNESCO World Heritage site; Marinella di Selinunte; Selinunte Archaeological Park, the largest archaeological park in Europe; Agrigento, founded by the Greeks in the 6th century BC
**Day 5:** Villa Romana del Casale, one of the best-preserved Roman villas; Caltagirone, a historic town in central Sicily known for its ceramics; Ragusa, one of the most beautiful baroque towns in Sicily; Modica, a UNESCO site (Late Baroque towns of the Val di Noto), known as the capital of chocolate
**Day 6:** Marzamemi, a historic fishing village; Noto; Aci Castello castle; Aci Trezza; Catania, Sicily's second-largest city
**Day 7:** Catania; Transfer to the airport; Flight to Tbilisi at 17:40
**Day 8:** Arrival in Tbilisi at 01:35

Included:
- Flight from Yerevan to Italy
- Flights Catania–Istanbul–Tbilisi

# Entering Georgia in 2026: visa-free stay, insurance, passport

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/georgia-entry-rules-visa-insurance-2026/

Since 1 January 2026 every foreign tourist entering Georgia must hold health and accident insurance of at least 30,000 GEL that covers the whole stay. Citizens of 96 countries, including the EU, the USA, the UK, Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan, need no visa and may stay up to one full year. This is the situation as of October 2026.

This guide is for foreign visitors and for anyone inviting friends or family to Georgia. Every rule below comes from the consular website of Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or from the official legal database, Matsne.

## Mandatory travel insurance from 2026

Georgia's Law on Tourism says tourists visiting Georgia must have mandatory health and accident insurance. The details are set by Government Decree No 602 of 26 December 2025, which applies from 1 January 2026.

- Sum insured: at least 30,000 GEL.
- The insurer can be Georgian or foreign.
- The policy must cover your whole stay, from the day you enter until you leave, including arrival and departure days.
- Paper or electronic, in Georgian or English.
- At the border, an officer of the Patrol Police Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs may check that you hold a policy.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists what the policy must show: the parties, the covered territory, what is insured, start and end dates, the insured risks, the sum insured (limits), and the premium with its place and terms of payment. Many standard travel policies meet this, but check the amount and the dates.

Exempt are holders of diplomatic or special visas; holders of diplomatic, official, service or special passports; accredited diplomats and staff of international organisations with their accredited family members; people entering under international agreements of Georgia; and drivers in international road transport.

The decree does not set a fine. However, the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens says a foreigner may be refused entry without health and accident insurance. We found no official source saying you can buy a policy at the border, so buy it before you travel. We are a travel agency and do not sell insurance.

## Who can enter without a visa

Government Decree No 255 lists the countries whose citizens may enter Georgia without a visa and stay for a full year. The list includes all EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, the UK, the USA, Canada, Australia, Japan, Israel, Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova and others.

- Russia: no visa, up to 1 full year. The ministry's "Do I need a visa?" tool shows the same.
- Ukraine: no visa, up to 1 year. Ukrainians who entered before 24 February 2025 may stay until 24 February 2027.
- China: no visa, but only for 30 days and only for tourism.
- Citizens of the EU, Switzerland and Liechtenstein may also enter with a national ID card.

If your country is not on the list, you may still enter without a Georgian visa for 90 days in any 180 days if you hold a valid visa or residence permit of the USA, the UK, an EU or Schengen country or another listed country. Everyone else needs a visa; a short-term visa can be requested online at evisa.gov.ge, and the ministry says a decision on such an application takes up to 5 working days.

## Passport validity

Georgian law asks for a valid travel document. We did not find an official Georgian rule that the passport must be valid for a set number of months after your trip. Our advice: make sure it is valid for the whole stay, and check with your airline, as some ask for more.

## Children

The insurance decree has no exemption for children, so each child needs their own policy and their own valid travel document. If a child travels with one parent or with another adult, carry the birth certificate and a consent letter from the other parent. We did not find a separate Georgian rule on this, but your home country may ask for it when you leave.

## Quick checklist

- Check if you need a visa on geoconsul.gov.ge (Entering Georgia).
- Make sure your passport is valid for the whole trip.
- Buy insurance for everyone, children too: at least 30,000 GEL, for every day of the stay.
- Keep the policy on your phone and, better, on paper too.

## Travel in Georgia with us

Once you are here, join one of our day tours: a Tbilisi city tour, Mtskheta and Uplistsikhe, Kazbegi, Sighnaghi or David Gareja. Contact us and we will help you choose.

**Do I need travel insurance to enter Georgia in 2026?** Yes. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must hold health and accident insurance of at least 30,000 GEL covering the whole stay.

**Is a policy from a foreign insurer accepted?** Yes. The policy can be from a Georgian or foreign insurer, in Georgian or English, on paper or electronic.

**Do Russian citizens need a visa for Georgia?** No. Citizens of Russia may enter without a visa and stay up to one full year. The insurance rule applies to them too.

**How long can I stay in Georgia without a visa?** Citizens of the listed countries can stay up to one full year. Citizens of China can stay 30 days for tourism.

**How long must my passport be valid?** The law asks for a valid travel document. We found no official rule with a number of months, so keep it valid for the whole trip and check with your airline.

**Do children need insurance?** Yes. The decree has no exemption for children, so each child needs their own policy.

Sources:
- MFA of Georgia, Consular Department: Entering Georgia (mandatory insurance from 1 January 2026, visa categories, e-Visa): https://geoconsul.gov.ge/en/entering-georgia
- MFA of Georgia, Consular Department: Do I need a visa? (check by citizenship): https://geoconsul.gov.ge/en/entering-georgia-visa
- Government of Georgia Decree No 602 of 26 December 2025: rules and conditions of mandatory health and accident insurance of tourists entering Georgia (Matsne, in Georgian): https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/6728816
- Law of Georgia on Tourism, Article 2 (tourist definition) and Article 12 (mandatory insurance) (Matsne, English): https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/6012850
- Law of Georgia on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, Articles 4 and 11 (Matsne, English): https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/2278806
- Government of Georgia Decree No 255 of 5 June 2015: list of countries whose citizens may enter Georgia without a visa (Matsne, in Georgian): https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/2867361
- Decree No 255 amendment of 2023: citizens of China, 30 days for tourism (Matsne): https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/5916029

# Svaneti Guide: What to See in Mestia and Ushguli and How to Get There

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/svaneti-mestia-ushguli-guide/

The highlights of Upper Svaneti are Mestia, with its Svan towers and the Svaneti Museum of History and Ethnography, and Ushguli, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You reach Mestia by road via Zugdidi, or by a small plane from Natakhtari near Tbilisi. Plan at least 3 days.

## Where Svaneti is and why go

Upper Svaneti lies in north-west Georgia, high in the Greater Caucasus along the upper Enguri river. Its main town is Mestia, at about 1,500 m. Upper Svaneti has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996, mainly for its medieval villages and stone tower houses.

People come for mountain views, old villages and hiking in summer, and for skiing in winter.

## What to see in Mestia

- Svan towers — stone tower houses, most of them built between the 9th and 12th centuries. Many are easy to see from the centre of Mestia.
- Svaneti Museum of History and Ethnography — old manuscripts, icons and traditional Svan clothing.
- Chalaadi glacier — a fairly easy walk from Mestia through forest and across streams to the ice.
- Koruldi lakes — a longer hike with views of the Caucasus peaks. You need to be reasonably fit.

## Ushguli

Ushguli is the highest village in Svaneti, about 46 km from Mestia. It is a group of small villages (Zhibiani, Chvibiani, Chazhashi, Murqmeli and Lamjurishi) at about 2,100 m, at the foot of Mount Shkhara. You see old towers and the Lamaria church on the hill above Zhibiani.

The road to Ushguli is a mountain road and depends on the weather. In winter and after heavy rain it can be hard going or closed for a while. Check road conditions before you set off.

## How to get to Svaneti

- From Tbilisi by road — via Kutaisi and Zugdidi. Georgia's official tourism site puts the drive at about 8-10 hours.
- From Kutaisi — about 4-5 hours by road, according to the same source.
- From Batumi — up the coast to Zugdidi, then the mountain road to Mestia.
- From Zugdidi — Mestia is about 128 km north-east of Zugdidi. There is also a train from Tbilisi to Zugdidi.
- By air — Mestia has Queen Tamar Airport. Small planes fly from Natakhtari (near Tbilisi) and from Kutaisi, but not every day, and flights are often moved because of mountain weather.

Our Svaneti tour goes by bus and stops at the Enguri Dam on the way, so you don't have to drive the long mountain road yourself.

## When to go

For hiking and for Ushguli, the warm months are best: summer and early autumn, when roads and trails are easiest to use. In winter Svaneti is a ski area: Hatsvali and Tetnuldi are close to Mestia. The season usually opens at the end of December, and slopes open step by step as snow allows.

## How many days you need

The trip is long, so Svaneti does not work as a day trip. Plan at least 3 days: one for the drive and Mestia, one for Ushguli, one to get back. The official tourism site suggests 3-4 days in Mestia. Add more days if you want to hike.

## What to do next

Open our Svaneti tour page or message us on WhatsApp for the next dates and the programme.

**What is there to see in Svaneti?** In Mestia: the Svan towers and the Svaneti Museum of History and Ethnography, with the Chalaadi glacier nearby. About 46 km away is Ushguli, at the foot of Mount Shkhara.

**How do I get to Mestia from Batumi?** Drive up the coast to Zugdidi, then take the mountain road to Mestia. You can also join our group tour.

**How long is the drive from Tbilisi to Mestia?** About 8-10 hours, according to Georgia's official tourism site. Flying is faster, but flights do not run every day.

**How many days do I need in Svaneti?** At least 3 days to see Mestia and Ushguli without rushing. Allow more if you want to hike.

**Can you visit Ushguli in winter?** Ushguli is under snow for a large part of the year and the road can close in winter. Check conditions before you go.

**Is there skiing in Svaneti?** Yes. Hatsvali and Tetnuldi ski areas are near Mestia. The season usually opens at the end of December.

- Georgia National Tourism Administration: Domestic flights (Natakhtari and Kutaisi to Mestia): https://georgia.travel/coming-to-georgia/domestic-flights

# Georgia in Winter: Weather, Skiing, Kazbegi and What to See

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/georgia-in-winter/

Winter in Georgia is mild in the lowlands: Tbilisi's average January high is about 6-7 °C, and Batumi's January average is about 5 °C. The mountains get plenty of snow, and ski resorts such as Gudauri, Bakuriani, Mestia and Goderdzi usually run from late December to April. Cities, museums and wine regions stay open all winter.

## What winter is like in Georgia

The Greater Caucasus range blocks much of the cold air from the north, so winters in the lowlands are fairly mild. The weather differs a lot from one region to another.

- Tbilisi and the east — in the 1991-2020 normals, Tbilisi's average January high is 6.6 °C and the average low is −0.8 °C. Snow is not frequent and rarely stays long.
- Black Sea coast — Batumi's average January temperature is about 5.4 °C. Winters are damp and rainy; snow is rare.
- Mountains — lots of snow higher up. Some mountain villages are hard to reach in winter; Ushguli, for example, is under snow for a large part of the year.

## Where to ski

- Gudauri — at about 2,200 m, roughly 120 km from Tbilisi. The official tourism site gives the season as late December to late April, with January and February the best months.
- Bakuriani — at about 1,700 m in the Borjomi gorge. The gentle Didveli slopes are recommended for beginners and families. The narrow-gauge 'Kukushka' train links Borjomi and Bakuriani when it runs.
- Mestia (Svaneti) — Hatsvali, about 8 km from Mestia, and Tetnuldi, home to the longest ski run in the South Caucasus.
- Goderdzi (highland Adjara) — at about 2,000 m. It is the closest ski area to Batumi.

In the 2025-2026 season, Kokhta in Bakuriani opened on 20 December and lifts at the other resorts started on 27 December. Slopes open step by step as the snow allows, so exact dates change every year.

## Kazbegi in winter

In winter, Stepantsminda and Gergeti Trinity Church sit under snow, and the views are beautiful. The road goes over the Jvari Pass and through Gudauri. Our winter day tour goes to Gudauri, with free time at the resort for skiing, sledging or just a walk in the snow.

In winter the Gudauri-Kobi section of the road can close to all vehicles for a while because of avalanche risk, as announced by Georgia's Roads Department. When that happens, the Kazbegi tour may be moved or changed. The Upper Lars border crossing depends on the same road.

## Tbilisi in winter

Winter is a good time to explore Tbilisi: the old town, Narikala, museums and restaurants. In Abanotubani, below Narikala, are the famous sulphur baths, and a warm bath on a cold day is one of the nicest parts of a winter trip. The baths are part of our Tbilisi city tour.

## What still works in winter

- Cities — Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi.
- Mtskheta and Uplistsikhe, Kakheti and its wine cellars — they are in the lowlands, so you can visit them in winter too.
- Ski resorts and Borjomi park.
- High mountain trails, some passes and remote villages are often closed or hard to reach.

## What to wear

For Tbilisi, a warm jacket is usually enough. For the mountains, bring a winter jacket, hat, gloves and shoes with non-slip soles. The mountain sun is strong, so pack sunglasses and sun cream too.

## What to do next

Pick a winter tour below or message us on WhatsApp. We will tell you which trips are possible right now, given the weather and the roads.

**What is the weather like in Georgia in winter?** Mild in the lowlands: Tbilisi's average January high is about 6-7 °C and Batumi's January average is about 5 °C. The mountains are cold and snowy.

**When does the ski season start in Gudauri?** Usually at the end of December. In 2025-2026 the lifts started on 27 December. The exact date depends on the snow each year.

**Which ski resort is best for children?** The official tourism site recommends the gentle Didveli slopes in Bakuriani for families and beginners.

**Can you visit Kazbegi in winter?** Yes, but the Gudauri-Kobi section sometimes closes because of avalanche risk. Check the road before you set off.

**What is there to do in Georgia in winter?** Tbilisi and its sulphur baths, snowy Kazbegi, skiing in Gudauri, Bakuriani or Svaneti, and wine cellars in Kakheti.

# Georgia with Kids: Where to Go and Practical Tips for Families

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/georgia-with-kids/

Children usually love Sataplia with its dinosaur footprints, Prometheus Cave, the Batumi Botanical Garden and the sea, Borjomi park and Bakuriani. Choose tours with short walks, pack water, snacks and a warm layer, and remember that mountain day tours take the whole day.

## What works for families

With children, what matters is short walks, something fun at each stop and not too many hours on the road. Below are places families usually enjoy, and the tours of ours that include them.

## Kutaisi and the caves

- Sataplia — a reserve about 10 km from Kutaisi, with dinosaur footprints, a cave and a glass viewing platform over the cliff. For many children this is the highlight of the trip.
- Prometheus Cave — a large cave with stalactites. About 1.8 km is open to visitors, so children will need to walk. It is cool inside; bring a jacket.
- Martvili and Okatse canyons — paths and views over water. Hold small children's hands on the trails.

Our Kutaisi caves and canyons tour covers these places, and from Batumi there is our Prometheus Cave, Sataplia and Kutaisi trip.

## Batumi and the sea

In summer many families choose Batumi: the sea, the boulevard and the Botanical Garden on the Green Cape. The warmest months in Batumi are July and August, with an average temperature of about 23 °C. Our Batumi city tour combines the boulevard and the Botanical Garden.

## Borjomi and Bakuriani

Borjomi Central Park is an easy place for a walk, with mineral springs. The small 'Kukushka' train climbs from Borjomi to Bakuriani when it runs. In winter, the official tourism site recommends Bakuriani's gentle Didveli slopes for beginners and families.

## Tbilisi and Kazbegi

The Tbilisi tour is on foot through the old town, Narikala and Abanotubani. With small children, a stroller is not always easy on the old town streets.

The Kazbegi tour leaves at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. The path to the small Gveleti waterfall is easy, about 500 m; the big waterfall is 1.2 km one way and of medium difficulty. If your child gets tired, you can skip the big waterfall.

## Practical tips

- Pick a tour whose travel time suits your child's age. Mountain tours are long.
- Pack water, snacks, wet wipes and a toy or book for the road.
- Dress in layers: mountains and caves are cool, the lowlands are hot in summer.
- The mountain sun is strong: hat, sunglasses, sun cream.
- If your child gets car sick, ask a doctor beforehand and tell us, so we can try to seat you near the front.
- For trips abroad, see our Booking terms page for documents for minors.

## What to do next

Below you will find tours that families often enjoy. Not sure which suits your child's age? Message us on WhatsApp and we will suggest one.

**Where to go in Georgia with kids?** Sataplia for the dinosaur footprints, Prometheus Cave, Batumi for the sea and the Botanical Garden, Borjomi and Bakuriani.

**Which tour is best for small children?** Tours with short walks: city tours, Sataplia, Borjomi park. The Kazbegi tour takes the whole day and can be tiring for little ones.

**How much walking is there in Prometheus Cave?** About 1.8 km is open to visitors. Bring a jacket, it is cool inside.

**When is the best time for Batumi with children?** July and August are the warmest months for the sea. September and October are the wettest months in Batumi.

**Can children ski in Georgia?** Yes. Bakuriani's gentle Didveli slopes are recommended for beginners and families.
