# Best Time to Visit Georgia: Seasons and Months Explained

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/best-time-to-visit-georgia/

For sightseeing and cities, the best times are late spring (May-June) and autumn (September-October). For the sea and the high mountains, choose July and August. The grape harvest (Rtveli) starts in Kakheti in September, and skiing usually runs from late December to April.

## In short: which season for what

- Sightseeing, cities, monasteries — May-June and September-October.
- Beach (Batumi, Adjara) — July and August.
- High mountains (Kazbegi, Juta, Svaneti) — summer and early autumn.
- Wine and the grape harvest — September-October in Kakheti.
- Skiing — late December to April.

## Spring (March-May)

In spring the lowlands turn green and the weather in the cities is pleasant. It is a good time for Tbilisi, Mtskheta, Kakheti and the semi-desert areas before the hot days start. In Batumi, spring is the driest time of year. High in the mountains there is still snow in March and April, and some roads and trails stay closed.

## Summer (June-August)

Summer is the season for the sea and the mountains. The warmest months in Batumi are July and August, with an average temperature of about 23 °C. Tbilisi is hot: the average July high is about 31 °C, so city walks are best in the morning or evening.

In the mountains this is the easiest time to walk: Kazbegi, Truso, Juta, Svaneti and Ushguli. Our Juta tour is a summer tour.

## Autumn (September-November)

For many people autumn is the best time in Georgia. The heat eases, the forests change colour and the grape harvest begins. According to Georgia's official tourism site, Rtveli starts in September with the Rkatsiteli harvest in Kakheti and runs until December, when Chkhaveri is picked in Guria and Adjara. A Kakheti wine tour is especially nice in September and October.

In Batumi, September to November are the wettest months of the year. If you go to the coast in autumn, have a plan for rainy days. The first snow can fall in the high mountains in late autumn.

## Winter (December-February)

Winter is mild in the lowlands: Tbilisi's average January high is about 6-7 °C. It is ski season: Gudauri, Bakuriani, Mestia and Goderdzi usually run from late December to April. Kazbegi is beautiful under snow, but the road sometimes closes because of avalanche risk. We cover winter in more detail in a separate article.

## For sightseeing tours

If your main goal is to see a lot of places, choose May-June or September-October. It is neither too hot nor too cold, and most mountain roads are open.

## What to do next

Below are our tours for different seasons. If you already know your dates, message us on WhatsApp and we will suggest what works best at that time.

**When is the best time to visit Georgia?** For sightseeing: May-June and September-October. For the sea and high mountains: July and August. For skiing: late December to April.

**When is beach season in Batumi?** July and August are the warmest months. September to November bring the most rain in Batumi.

**When is Rtveli, the grape harvest?** According to the official tourism site, it starts in Kakheti in September and continues until December in western Georgia.

**Is October a good time to visit Georgia?** Yes, October is good for sightseeing and for Kakheti. On the coast it is already rainy.

**When should I go to the mountains in Georgia?** In summer and early autumn, when roads and trails are open. In winter the mountains are for skiing.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Climate of Georgia (regional overview; Tbilisi 1991-2020 normals from Pogoda.ru.net): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_Georgia_(country)
- Wikipedia: Batumi (climate table, NCEI WMO normals 1981-2010): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batumi
- Georgia National Tourism Administration: Rtveli in Georgia: https://georgia.travel/rtveli-in-georgia
- Georgia National Tourism Administration: Winter resorts in Georgia: https://georgia.travel/winter-resorts-in-georgia
- Wikipedia: Ushguli (snow cover): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushguli

# Truso Valley Day Trip from Tbilisi: Travertines, Ketrisi, Zakagori

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/truso-valley-day-trip/

Our Truso tour leaves Tbilisi at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. In the valley you walk 6-7 km one way on an easy path. On the way you see colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Ketrisi village, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress.

## Where the Truso valley is

The Truso valley lies in Kazbegi municipality, in the historic Khevi region, on the north side of the main Caucasus watershed. The Terek (Tergi) river starts here. The valley runs about 25 km from the Truso Pass down to the village of Kobi, and its lowest part, near Kobi, is at about 2,000 m above sea level.

According to Georgia's national tourism site, the valley is about 22 km from Stepantsminda, and Stepantsminda is about 157 km from Tbilisi. So a good part of the day is spent on the road.

## What you see

- Colourful travertines: orange and reddish formations left by the valley's mineral springs. The valley is known for its mineral water.
- The 'bottomless' lake, one of the stops on our tour.
- Ketrisi village. The valley has more than ten abandoned villages and many towers, and Ketrisi is one of them. A well-known mineral spring carries its name.
- Abano Convent. Abano is also the name of one of the valley's well-known mineral springs.
- Zakagori Fortress, a fortress complex not far from the Russian border.

Do not climb or step on the travertines. The official tourism site warns that this damages them.

## How hard is the walking?

Our tour data gives the walk as 6-7 km one way. The path is easy, with no big climbs, but it is long. Remember that you also need to get back, so pace yourself for the whole day.

This trip suits people who can walk at a steady pace for several hours. If walking is hard for you or you have knee or foot problems, ask us before you book. The valley is high, so you may feel tired sooner than in the city.

## When to go

Truso is a high mountain valley, so the warm months are the best time. In the cold season snow and ice make walking hard. Check the exact dates on the tour page or with us.

## What to wear and bring

Mountain weather changes fast and is cooler than in Tbilisi. Dress in layers you can easily take off or put on.

- Comfortable hiking or sports shoes with good grip. The path can be wet or muddy.
- A wind and rain jacket and a warm jumper.
- Sunglasses, a hat and sunscreen: the sun is stronger up high.
- Water and food for the whole day. Meals are not listed in the tour data.
- Your ID card or passport. The valley is a border area, and you need a permit to go beyond Zakagori Fortress.
- A power bank.

## Truso or Kazbegi?

The Truso tour is mostly about walking: a quiet valley, abandoned villages and nature. The Kazbegi tour shows you more places with less walking: Dariali Monastery, the Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. Its longest walk is to the big waterfall, 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty. If you like walking, choose Truso. If you want to see a lot with less effort, choose Kazbegi.

## What to do next

The tour page has the price and the latest details. Book your seat early and check the mountain forecast the day before.

**How far do I walk in Truso?** According to the tour data, 6-7 km one way on an easy path. Plan for the way back too.

**What time does the tour leave and return?** It leaves at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00.

**Which document should I bring?** Bring your ID card or passport. The valley is a border area, and a permit is needed to go beyond Zakagori Fortress.

**Can I walk on the travertines?** No. Walking on them damages them, so enjoy them from the path.

**Does the Truso tour include Gergeti Trinity Church?** No, Gergeti is not on the Truso route. If you want to see it, choose our Kazbegi tour.

Sources:
- Georgia Travel (Georgian National Tourism Administration): Upper Truso Gorge: https://georgia.travel/en_US/mtskheta-mtianeti/kazbegi/Upper-Truso-Gorge
- Wikipedia (ka): თრუსოს ხეობა (length, lowest point, mineral springs): https://ka.wikipedia.org/wiki/თრუსოს_ხეობა
- Wikipedia: Truso Gorge (location, Terek source, border region): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truso_Gorge
- Wikipedia: Stepantsminda (distance from Tbilisi): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepantsminda

# David Gareja and the Colourful Mountains: What to See and Bring

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/david-gareja-colorful-mountains/

David Gareja is a rock-cut monastery complex founded in the 6th century, about 60-70 km southeast of Tbilisi in semi-desert. Our colourful desert tour combines the monasteries with the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains, with only about 1 km of easy walking in total. Summers here are very hot, so bring water, a hat and sunscreen.

## What David Gareja is

The David Gareja monastery complex lies in Kakheti, in Sagarejo municipality, on the semi-desert slopes of Mount Gareja at the edge of the Iori Plateau, about 60-70 km southeast of Tbilisi. It was founded in the first half of the 6th century by Saint David, one of the Thirteen Assyrian Fathers.

The complex has hundreds of cells, churches, chapels and refectories, most of them cut into the rock. David's Lavra was expanded by his disciples Dodo and Lukiane. Dodo's Rka ('Dodo's horn') is named after Dodo, and Natlismtsemeli is named after John the Baptist. The complex was at its height from the late 11th to the early 13th century, when the Udabno, Bertubani and Chichkhituri monasteries were built and wall painting flourished.

Part of the complex lies on the Georgia-Azerbaijan border: Bertubani is on the Azerbaijani side, and parts of Udabno and Chichkhituri are disputed. On site, follow the tour escort's directions.

## The colourful mountains and Mravaltskaro

The Gareja semi-desert has striped red and yellow hills that people call the colourful or rainbow mountains. Georgia's national tourism site describes Mravaltskaro reservoir, where the hills and sky are reflected in the water, and notes that many people call the place 'Georgian Mars'. The site places the reservoir in Gardabani municipality, in Kvemo Kartli.

## Our two tours: which to choose

- Colourful desert and David Gareja: Dodo's Rka, the David Gareja monastery complex, the colourful mountains, the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains and reservoir, the Monastery of St John the Baptist and views over the desert. About 1 km of easy walking in total. Leaves at 08:00, back at about 22:00.
- Sabereebi: the Sabereebi complex of Gareja (9th-10th centuries), with groups of rock-cut caves. Leaves at 08:00, back at about 23:00.

If it is your first visit and you want both monasteries and colourful landscapes in one day, choose the colourful desert tour. If you have already seen Gareja or are especially interested in cave monasteries, choose Sabereebi. Both tours include minibus transport, a tour escort and photography.

## Walking and heat

There is little walking on the colourful desert tour and it is easy, but the paths are stony and sloping in places. Gareja is semi-desert: there is almost no shade and midday in summer is very hot. If you do not cope well with heat, go in spring or autumn.

Georgia's national tourism site says the Gareja semi-desert is especially beautiful in late spring, when fresh grass comes up through the red soil. Our Gareja tours run in any weather and are postponed only if there is a problem with the road. After rain the ground can be muddy and slippery.

## What to bring

- Plenty of water, more than usual in summer.
- A hat, sunglasses and sunscreen.
- Closed shoes with good grip for stony paths.
- Light clothes that cover shoulders and knees. To enter a monastery, women need a headscarf and a skirt, men long trousers.
- Snacks. Meals are not listed in the tour data.
- Your ID card or passport, as the complex is close to the border.
- In spring and autumn, a warm layer: mornings and evenings in the desert are cool.

Stay on the paths, especially near cliff edges and on the border side. The soil on the colourful hills is loose and slippery.

## What to do next

Pick a tour, check the price and latest details on the tour page and book your seat early. If you cannot decide which Gareja trip suits you, write to us.

**How much walking is there?** On the colourful desert tour, about 1 km in total, easy. The Sabereebi tour data gives no distance, so ask us when you book.

**When is the best time to visit Gareja?** Spring and autumn are the most comfortable. Summer is very hot and there is almost no shade.

**What should I wear for the monastery?** Women need a headscarf and a skirt, men long trousers. Shoulders and knees should be covered.

**Which tour is best for a first visit?** The colourful desert and David Gareja tour, because it includes both the monasteries and the colourful mountains.

**Does the tour run in the rain?** Yes. It runs in any weather and is postponed only if there is a problem with the road.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: David Gareji monastery complex (founding, location, history, border): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Gareji_monastery_complex
- Wikipedia: Sagarejo Municipality (David Gareja section): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagarejo_Municipality
- Georgia Travel (Georgian National Tourism Administration): Mravaltskaro Reservoir: https://georgia.travel/mravaltskaro-reservoir

# Kakheti Day Trips from Tbilisi: Four Routes and Who Each Suits

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/kakheti-day-trips-from-tbilisi/

We run four Kakheti day routes: Sighnaghi and Bodbe; Ujarma to Alaverdi; Nekresi, Gremi and Telavi; and Gurjaani and Zegaani. Sighnaghi and Bodbe is best for a first visit, the Alaverdi route for monastery lovers, Gremi and Telavi for history fans, and Gurjaani and Zegaani for people who have already seen the classic sights.

## What all four routes have in common

All four tours leave Tbilisi at 08:00 and are back at about 23:00. We travel by minibus with a tour escort. The tours run in any weather and are postponed only if there is a problem with the road. Walking is light on every route, mostly around the sites and town streets.

## 1. Sighnaghi and Bodbe: for a first visit

Route: Ninotsminda monastery complex, Manavi Fortress, the Bodbe Convent of St Nino and Sighnaghi.

- Ninotsminda Cathedral was built around 575. It collapsed after earthquakes in 1824 and 1848, and only the eastern apse and part of the western wall survive. The bell tower dates from the 16th century, the reign of King Levan.
- Bodbe Monastery stands, by tradition, over the grave of St Nino. The first monastery was built in the 9th century, and today it is a convent about 2 km from Sighnaghi.
- Sighnaghi is about 113 km from Tbilisi. The town is ringed by remains of 18th-century walls and looks out over the Alazani Valley. It is known as the 'City of Love'.

Who it suits: first-time visitors to Kakheti, families and older travellers. You get time to stroll the streets of Sighnaghi and enjoy the views. Meals are not included on this tour.

## 2. Ujarma to Alaverdi: the classic monasteries

Route: Ujarma fortress-town, Gombori Pass, Shuamta convent and monastery, Ikalto monastery complex, Tetri Giorgi and Alaverdi. The road crosses the Gombori range: from Tbilisi to Telavi this way is about 96 km, compared with about 156 km on the main highway.

- Ujarma fortress stands 4 km north of Ujarma village, near the Gombori Pass. It dates to the reign of King Aspagur (3rd-4th centuries) and was later strengthened by Vakhtang Gorgasali.
- Old Shuamta has a 5th-century basilica and two 7th-century domed churches. New Shuamta was founded by the wife of King Levan.
- The Academy of Ikalto was founded between the 11th and 13th centuries. Its first rector was Arsen of Ikalto.
- Alaverdi's Cathedral of St George was built in the 11th century under King Kvirike III of Kakheti. It is over 55 m tall and was the tallest church in Georgia until 2004.

Who it suits: people who love churches, old architecture and mountain-road views.

## 3. Nekresi, Gremi and Telavi: the Kakhetian kingdom

Route: Nekresi monastery complex, Ilia Lake, Gremi and the Batonis Tsikhe complex in Telavi.

- Nekresi Monastery stands on a hill in the foothills of the Greater Caucasus, between Kvareli and the village of Shilda. Monastic life here began in the 6th century, and the monastery is still active. It is linked to Abibos of Nekresi, one of the Thirteen Assyrian Fathers.
- Gremi was the capital of the Kingdom of Kakheti in the 16th and 17th centuries. King Levan built the Church of the Archangels in 1565. In 1615 the town was destroyed by the army of Shah Abbas I. The bell tower houses a museum.
- Batonis Tsikhe in Telavi is a 17th-century fortress and royal palace. King Erekle II was born and died in Telavi.

Who it suits: history lovers and anyone who wants to see Kakheti's old royal capitals. Nekresi Monastery is on a hill, so if uphill walking is hard for you, ask us before you book.

## 4. Gurjaani and Zegaani: lesser-known Kakheti

Route: Chailuri (Niakhura) Fortress (16th century), Gurjaani Kvelatsminda (8th-9th centuries), the Nato Vachnadze House-Museum, Ziari Lake, Zegaani Monastery (5th-9th centuries) and the Sanagire monastery complex (10th-11th centuries).

Gurjaani Kvelatsminda is the only surviving two-domed church in Georgia. This tour meets at Didube metro station.

Who it suits: people who have already seen Sighnaghi and Alaverdi and want another side of Kakheti, and fans of Georgian cinema, who will enjoy the Nato Vachnadze House-Museum.

## Other day trips in Kakheti

- David Gareja: the colourful desert tour (monasteries plus the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains, about 1 km of walking in total) or the Sabereebi cave monasteries.
- Lagodekhi: a hike to the Ninoskhevi (Gurgeniani) waterfall, 8.3 km one way, medium and hard in places. This tour leaves at 07:00.

## What to bring

- Comfortable shoes: monastery yards and Sighnaghi's streets have cobbles and slopes.
- For monasteries: a headscarf and skirt for women, long trousers for men.
- Water and money for food. Meals are not listed in the tour data.
- A hat and sunscreen in summer, a warm jacket in winter: the Gombori Pass is colder than Tbilisi.

## What to do next

Pick a route, check the price and latest details on the tour page and book your seat early. If you plan to visit Kakheti more than once, start with Sighnaghi or Alaverdi, then do Gremi and Gurjaani.

**Which Kakheti tour is best for a first visit?** Sighnaghi and Bodbe: Ninotsminda, Manavi Fortress, Bodbe Monastery and Sighnaghi. There is little walking and it suits all ages.

**What time do the tours leave and return?** All four routes leave at 08:00 and are back at about 23:00.

**Do the tours run in bad weather?** Yes. The Kakheti tours run in any weather and are postponed only if there is a problem with the road.

**Which tour includes Alaverdi?** The classic Kakheti route, together with Ujarma, Shuamta and Ikalto.

**Are meals included?** Meals are not included on the Sighnaghi tour and are not listed for the others. Budget for food.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Sighnaghi (distance from Tbilisi, fortifications, Alazani Valley): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sighnaghi
- Wikipedia: Bodbe Monastery: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodbe_Monastery
- Wikipedia: Ninotsminda Cathedral: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninotsminda_Cathedral
- Wikipedia: Sagarejo Municipality (Ujarma fortress): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagarejo_Municipality
- Wikipedia: Old Shuamta: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Shuamta
- Wikipedia: Academy of Ikalto: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Ikalto
- Wikipedia: Alaverdi Monastery: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaverdi_Monastery
- Wikipedia: Nekresi: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nekresi
- Wikipedia: Gremi: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gremi
- Wikipedia: Telavi (Batonis Tsikhe, routes from Tbilisi): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telavi
- Wikipedia: Gurjaani Kvelatsminda Church: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurjaani_Kvelatsminda_Church

# Before You Travel: What Not to Forget Before Leaving Home

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/before-you-travel-checklist/

One or two weeks before departure, check your passport's validity and the entry rules, read your insurance policy, tell your bank you're travelling and sort out mobile data. In the last few days, make copies of your documents, download offline maps, check in for your flight and save emergency numbers, including the Consular Department hotline of Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

This list covers what to do before you leave home. For what to put in your bag, see our separate article, 'Group Tour Checklist: Documents and Packing for Travel from Georgia'.

## Passport and entry rules

Start with your passport. Our booking terms require it to be valid for at least 6 months after the trip ends. If it isn't, apply for a new one early: it takes time, and the last week before a trip is often too late.

Next, check whether the country needs a visa or an electronic travel authorisation. We have separate articles on this: 'Schengen Without a Visa for Georgians: 90/180, Documents, ETIAS', 'Egypt Visa for Georgian Citizens', 'Turkey with a Georgian ID Card', 'Entering Armenia from Georgia: ID Card or Passport?', plus articles on visas for Jordan, Morocco, India, China and Sri Lanka. Rules change, so check once more with an official source or the embassy before you go.

If you need an e-visa, apply in good time and keep the approved visa both on your phone and on paper.

## Travel insurance: what to read in the policy

Travel insurance is included in our flight tours (see the 'included' list on the tour page). It usually covers urgent medical care abroad, but the details depend on the policy. Read it at least once before you go and find out four things:

- Which number to call if you need a doctor (the insurer's or its partner's hotline).
- What isn't covered. Look for the 'exclusions' section: it may list things like flare-ups of chronic conditions or risky activities.
- Whether there is a deductible, the amount you pay yourself.
- Whether you must call the insurer first, or can see a doctor first and claim the cost back later.

Save the policy on your phone and the hotline number in your contacts. If you take regular medication or have a chronic condition, ask the insurer in advance how the policy handles it.

## Bank and cards

Tell your bank you're going abroad, or check in your banking app that card payments abroad and online are switched on. Check your limits and your card's expiry date. Save the bank's hotline number so you can block a lost card quickly. We cover this in more detail in 'Money Abroad: Card or Cash, Currency, ATMs and Extra Costs'.

## Mobile data and phone

- Roaming: ask your operator what data and calls cost in the country you're visiting. In some countries it's expensive, so keep mobile data roaming off until you know the price.
- Local SIM card: often cheaper, but buying one takes time on arrival, and some countries ask for your passport.
- eSIM: you can buy and activate one from home. First check that your phone supports eSIM.
- Keep your Georgian number active if your bank sends SMS codes to confirm payments.

## Copies of documents

Keep copies of your passport, visa, insurance policy and tickets in two places: on paper (separate from the passport) and on your phone. Save the files so they open without internet. Send copies to a family member as well, in case you lose your phone.

## Offline maps and useful apps

- Maps: download the cities you'll visit so the map works offline.
- Translator: download the language you need for offline use.
- Your airline's app, which shows flight changes and your boarding pass.
- Taxi and public transport apps that work in your destination.
- A currency converter, so you can check prices in lari quickly.

## Check-in and getting to the airport

On a group tour the escort helps with tickets and check-in, but a few things are worth knowing yourself:

- Online check-in opens a set time before the flight. Some low-cost airlines charge for check-in at the airport, so read your ticket terms in advance.
- Save your boarding pass on your phone and, ideally, print it too.
- Be at the airport at the time the tour escort gives you. If you fly on your own, check your airline's advice and allow time for traffic.
- On some of our Kutaisi tours, the transfer from Tbilisi to the airport isn't included. Check the 'not included' list on the tour page and plan the journey.

## Your home

- Leave a key with a neighbour or relative you trust.
- Ask someone to water your plants.
- Unplug appliances, lock the windows and, if you can, turn off the water and gas.
- Clear perishable food from the fridge and take out the rubbish.
- Pay utility bills and loan instalments in advance so nothing falls due while you're away.

## Emergency numbers and the Georgian consulate

Save these numbers on your phone and write them down on paper too:

- 112, the EU emergency number. According to the European Commission, it is free in every EU country and connects you to the police, ambulance and fire service. Outside the EU, look up the local emergency number before you go.
- The hotline of the Consular Department of Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs: (+995 32) 2 94 50 50 (as listed on the consular portal, as of October 2026).
- The address and phone number of the Georgian embassy or consulate in your destination. You'll find them on the consular portal, geoconsul.gov.ge, under consular offices.
- Your insurer's and your bank's hotlines.
- The tour escort's number, and the number of a family member who should be contacted if needed.

The consular portal also has useful information about each country and a consular registration service. Leave your itinerary and hotel names with a family member.

## What to do next

Choose a tour and check your passport's validity before booking. A week before departure, go through this list once more. If anything is unclear, ask us when you book.

**What should I do a week before departure?** Check your passport and visa, read your insurance policy, tell your bank you're travelling and sort out mobile data: roaming, a local SIM or an eSIM.

**Where can I find the Georgian embassy's number abroad?** On the consular portal, geoconsul.gov.ge, under consular offices. The Consular Department hotline of Georgia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is (+995 32) 2 94 50 50.

**Which number do I call in an emergency in Europe?** In EU countries, call 112. It's free and connects you to the police, ambulance and fire service.

**Do I need paper copies if my documents are on my phone?** Yes, it's a good idea. A phone can be lost or run out of battery, so keep a paper copy separate from your passport.

**Is insurance included in the tour price?** Travel insurance is included in our flight tours. Check the 'included' list on the tour page and read the policy terms before you go.

Sources:
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia: Consular portal (consular offices, consular registration, Consular Department hotline): https://geoconsul.gov.ge/en
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia: About the consular portal (Consulate General in Odesa page): https://odessa.mfa.gov.ge/en/consular-portal
- European Commission: 112, the EU's emergency phone number: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/112

# Hand Luggage on Low-Cost Flights from Kutaisi: What Fits and What Doesn't

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/hand-luggage-low-cost-flights/

Most of our Kutaisi tours include one piece of hand luggage: 10 kg, 40x30x20 cm. That's the size of a small backpack, not a cabin trolley. Pack liquids in containers of up to 100 ml in one clear 1-litre bag, and keep your power bank in your hand luggage or on you.

## How big is 40x30x20 cm?

Think of the backpack you carry around town. A wheeled cabin suitcase usually won't fit these measurements. Everything that sticks out counts: outer pockets, handles and wheels.

- Measure the bag when it's full: soft backpacks bulge once packed.
- Weigh it at home. A luggage scale is cheap and saves trouble at the airport.
- Choose a light bag: a heavy one eats into your 10 kg.

The exact terms are on your ticket. Airline rules change, and if your bag is too big or too heavy you may be charged at the airport. If you need more luggage, tell us when you book.

## What fits for a 4-5 day trip

A bag this size holds what you need for 4-5 days if you leave the extras at home:

- 2-3 T-shirts or shirts and one warm layer that go together;
- one pair of trousers or a skirt in the bag, the other on you;
- underwear and socks for each day;
- a light jacket or an umbrella, depending on the season;
- a small pouch for documents, phone and charger;
- medicines in their original packaging.

Roll your clothes rather than folding them; they take less space. Stuff socks into your shoes so no space is wasted. Wear your heaviest shoes and jacket on the journey.

## Liquids: the 100 ml rule

According to the European Commission, at EU airports you can take liquids, aerosols and gels in your hand luggage only like this:

- each container holds no more than 100 ml;
- all of them fit into one transparent, resealable 1-litre plastic bag;
- medicines and special dietary items you need during the trip, including baby food, are exempt;
- duty-free liquids bought at the airport or on board are also exempt if they stay in a sealed security bag with the receipt inside.

Shampoo, cream, lotion, toothpaste and perfume all count as liquids. When you fly out of Kutaisi, screening is done by Kutaisi airport's security service; on the way back it's a European airport, where the rules above apply. So it's simplest to pack your liquids this way for the whole trip. Put the bag on top so you can take it out quickly at security.

Wine, oil or any other liquid in a container over 100 ml won't get through security in hand luggage. If you only have hand luggage, buy such souvenirs in the airport duty-free shop or add checked baggage in advance.

## Power banks and electronics

Under a May 2025 bulletin from the EU Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), a power bank counts as a spare battery and is not allowed in checked baggage. Keep it on you or in your hand luggage.

- Protect it from short circuits: keep it in its original packaging or a separate pouch.
- Pack it away from perfume and other flammable items.
- The bulletin asks airlines to tell passengers that power banks must not be used to charge devices during the flight.
- Check the capacity (Wh) printed on it. The bulletin gives 100 Wh for electrically powered equipment, or 160 Wh with the airline's approval. Your airline may be stricter.
- E-cigarettes also go only in hand luggage or on you.

If the cabin is full and your bag has to go in the hold at the aircraft door, take your power bank and spare batteries out and keep them with you.

## What not to pack in hand luggage

- Knives, large scissors, tools and other sharp or heavy items: these are generally not allowed in the cabin. Check the exact list on the airport's or airline's website.
- Liquids in containers over 100 ml, including a full water bottle.
- Spare shoes and 'just in case' items: they take up the most space.
- Valuables you won't need on the trip.

## When 10 kg isn't enough

Some of our tours include checked baggage. For example, our Egypt tours from Tbilisi include 20 kg of baggage, and the Sicily tour includes 20 kg checked baggage on top of 10 kg hand luggage. If you need more luggage on a Kutaisi tour, ask us when booking whether it can be added in advance.

## What to do next

Choose a tour, check the 'included' list to see what luggage you get, then pack, measure and weigh your bag at home. Our general list of documents and items is in 'Group Tour Checklist: Documents and Packing for Travel from Georgia'.

**How much hand luggage is included on tours from Kutaisi?** On most of our tours, one bag of 10 kg, 40x30x20 cm. Check the tour page and your ticket for the exact terms.

**Can I take a wheeled suitcase?** A standard cabin trolley usually doesn't fit 40x30x20 cm. If you need a bigger bag, ask us about extra luggage when you book.

**How much liquid can I take in hand luggage?** Each container up to 100 ml, all together in one clear 1-litre bag. Medicines and baby food are exempt.

**Where do I pack my power bank?** Only in your hand luggage or on you. Power banks are not allowed in checked baggage.

**Can I bring back a bottle of wine?** Not in hand luggage, unless you bought it in the airport duty-free shop and it stays in the sealed bag. Otherwise you'll need checked baggage.

Sources:
- European Commission (DG MOVE): Liquids, aerosols and gels in cabin baggage: https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/air/aviation-security/aviation-security-policy/liquids-aerosols-and-gels_en
- EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2025-03: Passenger and Crew Awareness on the Risks of Lithium Batteries (27 May 2025): https://ad.easa.europa.eu/blob/EASA_SIB_2025_03.pdf/SIB_2025-03_1

# Money Abroad: Card or Cash, Currency, ATMs and Extra Costs

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/money-abroad-cards-and-cash/

Take both: a card for hotels, shops and restaurants, and cash for small costs, markets and tips. Take euros for Europe and US dollars for our Egypt tours, where the visa and optional excursions are priced in dollars. Before you go, check your card's terms with your bank, and budget for optional excursions and museums in advance.

## Card or cash?

The best answer is both. A card is safer and means you don't carry large sums; cash helps where cards aren't accepted or the terminal isn't working.

- By card: hotels, shops, restaurants, transport tickets, museums.
- In cash: markets, small cafés, public toilets, tips and some optional excursions.
- Keep a backup card separate from your main one, so you have another if one is lost or blocked.

## Which currency to take

- Eurozone countries (Greece, Italy, Spain, Portugal, France, Malta, Lithuania, Slovakia, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Austria): euro.
- Switzerland: Swiss franc.
- Turkey: Turkish lira. On our Cappadocia tour, optional activities are priced in euros.
- Egypt: Egyptian pound. On our tours, the visa and optional excursions are priced in US dollars.

Lari is often hard to exchange abroad, so buy euros or dollars in Georgia. If the local currency isn't the euro, you can buy it on arrival or withdraw it from an ATM.

## Where and how to exchange money

The National Bank of Georgia publishes the official lari exchange rate every day. As the National Bank explains, this rate is indicative and its use is not obligatory, except where the law requires it. Banks and exchange offices set their own buying and selling rates, so:

- compare rates at a few places and see how far they are from the official rate;
- ask whether there's an extra fee for the exchange;
- rates at tourist spots and airports may be less favourable, so check before you exchange;
- never change money with strangers on the street.

## ATMs and fees

When you withdraw cash abroad, two parties may charge you: your bank and the ATM's owner. Find out your bank's fee before you travel. Read the messages on the ATM screen carefully and confirm only after that.

Sometimes an ATM or card terminal offers to charge you in lari. This is called dynamic currency conversion. Under EU rules, the merchant must show you the cost of this service before you pay, as a mark-up over the European Central Bank's rate. Compare it with your bank's terms before you agree. If you don't know which is cheaper, ask your bank before you leave.

Use ATMs inside or next to a bank branch where possible. Cover the keypad with your hand when you enter your PIN.

## Sort things out with your bank

- Switch on card payments abroad and online, if your bank requires this separately.
- Check your daily limits for both payments and cash withdrawals.
- Find out the fees for paying in foreign currency and for ATM withdrawals.
- Make sure your bank's SMS codes will reach you abroad.
- Save the bank's hotline and learn how to block your card in the app.

## Tipping

Tipping customs differ from country to country. In some places service is already included in the bill; in others a tip is expected. Read the bill carefully and, if you don't know the local custom, ask the tour escort or guide. Keep some small change in local currency for tips.

## Keeping your money safe

- Split your money and cards: the day's spending in your wallet, the rest in the hotel safe or an inside pocket of your bag.
- In crowds and on public transport, keep your bag in front of you.
- Don't count large sums in public.
- When paying, keep your card in sight.

If you enter or leave the EU carrying EUR 10,000 or more (or the same amount in other currencies), the European Commission says you must fill in a cash declaration at customs.

## Budget for optional extras

Not everything is included in the tour price. Read the 'not included' and optional-extras lists on the tour page and budget for them in advance. Examples from our tours:

- Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu (by bus): hot-air balloon flight 200–250 EUR and Turkish Night 30 EUR (both optional), local fees 300 GEL.
- Spain and Portugal: museum entry fees, optional, 100–150 EUR.
- Alsace and Paris: museum entry fees, optional, 130–150 EUR in total.
- Venice Carnival: museums 70–100 EUR, local transport 70–90 EUR, transfer 60 EUR.
- Sharm el-Sheikh and Petra: optional local tours from 30 to 100 USD, for example a yacht tour for 60 USD.

On most of our European tours only breakfast is included, so plan for lunch and dinner. On some Kutaisi tours the Tbilisi–Kutaisi transfer (60 GEL) is also paid separately.

These prices come from our current tour data and may change. Check the exact amounts on the tour page or ask us when you book.

## What to do next

Choose a tour, see what isn't included and work out how much cash you'll need. Then check your card's terms with your bank. For the rest of your pre-trip to-do list, see 'Before You Travel: What Not to Forget Before Leaving Home'.

**Which currency should I take to Europe?** Euros for eurozone countries. Switzerland's currency is the Swiss franc.

**Is it better to exchange money in Georgia?** Buy euros or dollars in Georgia: lari is often hard to exchange abroad. Local currency, such as the Egyptian pound, can be bought on arrival.

**The terminal offers to charge me in lari. Should I accept?** First look at the cost it shows and compare it with your bank's terms. If you're not sure, ask your bank before you travel.

**How much cash should I take?** It depends on the route. Add up the 'not included' items and any optional extras you want, plus meals and small costs, and take in cash what you can't pay by card.

**Do I need to declare cash at the border?** When entering or leaving the EU, yes, if you carry EUR 10,000 or more. Check other countries' rules separately.

Sources:
- National Bank of Georgia: Official exchange rate of the lari (indicative, not obligatory): https://nbg.gov.ge/en/monetary-policy/currency
- Your Europe (European Union): Electronic and cash payments, dynamic currency conversion: https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/finance-funding/making-receiving-payments/electronic-cash-payments/index_en.htm
- European Commission (DG TAXUD): EU cash controls, EUR 10 000 declaration: https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/customs/prohibitions-restrictions/eu-cash-controls_en

# Jordan Visa for Georgian Citizens: On Arrival and Jordan Pass (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/jordan-visa-for-georgians/

Georgian citizens need a visa for Jordan, but usually do not have to get it in advance: Georgia is not on the Jordanian Ministry of Interior's list of 'restricted' nationalities, so you get the visa on arrival at Amman airport. A single-entry visa costs 40 Jordanian dinars, and Jordan Pass holders who stay at least two nights pay no visa fee (as of October 2026).

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Jordan?

Yes, but it is easy to get. Jordan's Ministry of Interior splits countries into two groups: citizens of 'restricted' countries need prior approval to enter, citizens of 'non-restricted' countries do not. Georgia is not on the ministry's published list of restricted countries.

According to the official Jordan Pass website, citizens of non-restricted countries get a visa on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport in Amman and at the Sheikh Hussein Bridge (Jordan River) border crossing.

## How much does the Jordan visa cost?

According to the official Jordan Pass website, as of October 2026:

- Single-entry tourist visa without the Jordan Pass: 40 Jordanian dinars (about 60 USD, as the site puts it)
- The single-entry visa is valid for one month and can be extended at a police station for an extra fee

## The Jordan Pass: visa and entry tickets in one

The Jordan Pass is an official tourist pass. It covers entry to more than 40 sites, including Petra, Jerash and Wadi Rum, and it also covers the single-entry tourist visa fee. There are three versions:

- Jordan Wanderer: 70 dinars (one day in Petra)
- Jordan Explorer: 75 dinars (two consecutive days in Petra)
- Jordan Expert: 80 dinars (three consecutive days in Petra)

The visa fee is waived only if you buy the Jordan Pass before you arrive in Jordan and stay at least two full nights (three days). The airport immigration system checks this when you leave. The pass covers a single-entry visa only, not a multiple-entry one.

## Aqaba: a free visa when you arrive by sea

Aqaba is a special economic zone. The official tourism website of the zone's authority (ASEZA) says that visitors entering through Aqaba's port, airport or land border (except the southern Wadi Araba crossing) receive a free visa to Jordan. The condition: you must leave Jordan within one month through the same border.

The same site notes that some nationalities need a visa before travel and that the rules can change without notice, so check again before you go.

## Petra from Egypt: the ferry from Nuweiba to Aqaba

On our 8-day tour 'Egypt and Jordan: Sharm el-Sheikh and Petra' we visit Petra in one day. We leave by bus at night for the port of Nuweiba, take a ferry of about an hour to Aqaba and drive on to Petra. In the evening we take the ferry from Aqaba back to Nuweiba.

So you enter and leave Jordan through the same border, the port of Aqaba, on the same day. This matches the Aqaba special economic zone rule described above.

When you book, check two things with our manager: what is included for the Jordan part (for example, the Petra ticket and port fees), and which Egyptian visa you need. You re-enter Egypt from Jordan, and Egypt's official portal issues single-entry and multiple-entry visas separately.

## What to carry

- A valid passport (for our tours, valid for at least 6 months)
- Your Jordan Pass, if you bought one
- Hotel booking and return ticket
- Enough money for the visa or any fees paid on the spot

## Travel to Jordan with us

You can see Petra as part of our Egypt holiday: the 8-day programme combines a beach stay in Sharm el-Sheikh with a day trip to Petra. If you only want Egypt, look at our Cairo and Alexandria tour or our Hurghada tour. Each tour page shows what is included, and our manager will answer visa questions when you book.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Jordan?** Yes, but usually not in advance: Georgia is not on the 'restricted' list, and the visa is issued on arrival at Amman airport.

**How much is the Jordan visa?** As of October 2026 a single-entry tourist visa costs 40 Jordanian dinars and is valid for one month.

**Does the Jordan Pass cover the visa fee?** Yes, if you buy it before arrival and stay at least two full nights in Jordan. It covers a single-entry visa only.

**Do I pay for a visa if I arrive in Aqaba by ferry?** According to the official site of the Aqaba special economic zone, visitors arriving through Aqaba port get a free visa if they leave within one month through the same border.

**What should I check when booking the Petra trip?** What is included for the Jordan part, and which Egyptian visa you need, because you re-enter Egypt from Jordan.

Sources:
- Ministry of Interior of Jordan: Restricted and Non-Restricted Countries/Nationalities: https://moi.gov.jo/En/Pages/Restricted_and_Non_Restricted_Countries_Nationalities
- Jordan Pass (official): FAQ on visa on arrival, visa fee and the two-night rule: https://www.jordanpass.jo/Contents/FAQs.aspx
- Jordan Pass (official): packages and prices: https://www.jordanpass.jo/Contents/Prices.aspx
- Visit Aqaba, Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority (ASEZA): Visa and travel requirements: https://visitaqaba.com/EN/List/Visa
- Jordan government portal: Travel visas: https://jordan.gov.jo/EN/Pages/Travel_Visas

# Morocco Visa for Georgian Citizens: eVisa or Embassy Visa (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/morocco-visa-for-georgians/

Yes, Georgian citizens need a visa for Morocco. According to Morocco's official portal (acces-maroc.ma), a Georgian can get an eVisa only if they hold a valid multiple-entry visa from the Schengen area, the USA, the UK or another listed country; otherwise the visa is issued through an embassy or consulate. The Morocco visa is included in the price of our Morocco tour.

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Morocco?

Yes. The official portal of Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, acces-maroc.ma, has a form called 'Do I need a visa to enter Morocco?'. On 17 October 2026 we filled it in for a Georgian citizen living in Georgia, travelling on an ordinary passport for tourism.

The answer depends on whether the traveller holds another country's valid visa:

- No other visa: the portal points you to a regular visa issued through an embassy or consulate
- A valid visa from one of the listed countries: you can apply for an eVisa online

## Who can get the eVisa

According to the portal, a Georgian citizen can get an eVisa if they hold one of these visas:

- a Schengen visa
- a UK, USA or Ireland visa
- a Canada, Australia or New Zealand visa
- a Japan or Norway visa

That visa must be multiple-entry and valid for more than 90 days.

Georgian citizens travel to the Schengen area without a visa, so many of them do not have a Schengen visa. In that case the eVisa is not available and you need a regular visa.

## eVisa fee and processing time

As of October 2026 the portal offers two eVisa options:

- Standard: 770 Moroccan dirhams, processed in 3 to 7 business days
- Express: 1100 Moroccan dirhams, processed in 1 to 3 business days

The eVisa is single-entry and allows a stay of up to 30 days. The fee for a refused application is not refunded.

## What you confirm in the application

In the eVisa application the traveller confirms that they:

- are travelling for tourism
- have a return ticket
- have a hotel booking or an invitation
- have enough money, at least 70 EUR per day
- will still hold a valid passport when leaving Morocco

The portal also checks that your passport is valid for more than 90 days. For our tours, your passport must be valid for at least 6 months.

## If you do not have another country's visa

In this case the portal tells you to contact a Moroccan embassy or consulate and book an appointment. Check the list of documents and the processing times on the consular portal consulat.ma or with the embassy directly, as they can change.

## Morocco with us: the visa is included

The Morocco visa is included in the price of our 10-day group tour of Morocco with a stop in Rome. The programme covers Rome, Marrakesh, Ait Ben Haddou, Rabat, Chefchaouen, Fes and Casablanca. When you book, our manager will tell you which documents to bring for the visa and by what date.

Visa processing takes time, so book early and get your documents ready in good time.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Morocco?** Yes. According to Morocco's official portal, Georgian citizens need a visa.

**Can I get the Morocco eVisa?** Only if you hold a valid multiple-entry visa from the Schengen area, the UK, the USA, Ireland, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan or Norway, valid for more than 90 days.

**How much is the Morocco eVisa?** As of October 2026 the standard eVisa costs 770 dirhams and the express one 1100 dirhams.

**How long can I stay on the eVisa?** The eVisa is single-entry and allows a stay of up to 30 days.

**Is the visa included in your Morocco tour?** Yes, the Morocco visa is included in our 10-day tour of Morocco with a stop in Rome.

Sources:
- Accès Maroc, official visa and eVisa portal of the Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs (eligibility check): https://www.acces-maroc.ma/
- Accès Maroc portal data: eVisa prices, processing time and length of stay: https://api.acces-maroc.ma/evisa-api/api/referentiel/prixEvisa
- Consular portal of Morocco (Ministry of Foreign Affairs): https://www.consulat.ma/

# India Visa for Georgian Citizens: e-Visa Types, Fees and Timing (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/india-e-visa-for-georgians/

Georgian citizens need a visa for India, but they can get it online: Georgia is on the list of countries eligible for India's official e-Visa. As of October 2026 the 30-day e-Tourist Visa costs 25 USD from July to March and 10 USD from April to June, and the 1-year one 40 USD. Apply at least 4 days before you arrive.

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for India?

Yes. Georgian citizens cannot get a visa on arrival: according to the official portal, that option is only for citizens of Japan, South Korea and, under a condition, the UAE. Georgians can apply for an e-Visa on the official portal, indianvisaonline.gov.in. Georgia is on the portal's list of eligible countries.

## Types of e-Tourist Visa

- 30-day e-Tourist Visa: valid for 30 days from your first arrival in India, multiple entry, cannot be extended or converted
- 1-year e-Tourist Visa: valid for 365 days from the date it is granted, multiple entry
- 5-year e-Tourist Visa: valid for five years from the date it is granted, multiple entry

With the 1-year and 5-year visas you cannot stay in India for more than 180 days in total in one calendar year. The portal also offers business, medical, conference and other e-Visas.

## How much does the India visa cost for Georgians?

The e-Visa fee depends on your nationality. As of October 2026, the official fee table lists these amounts for Georgia:

- 30-day e-Tourist Visa (April to June): 10 USD
- 30-day e-Tourist Visa (July to March): 25 USD
- 1-year e-Tourist Visa: 40 USD
- 5-year e-Tourist Visa: 200 USD

A bank charge of 3% is added. The fee is not refunded, even if the visa is refused. The portal stresses that the Government of India charges no extra fee for an urgent visa and that nothing more is paid at the airport.

Our India tour lists a 'visa fee of 40 USD' as not included. That matches the 1-year visa; for the October group the 30-day visa costs 25 USD. Please confirm the exact amount and visa type with our manager when you book.

## When to apply

Apply for the e-Tourist Visa at least 4 days before your arrival and no earlier than 120 days before your trip. The fee must also be paid at least 4 days before travel, or the application will not be processed. The decision comes by email, and you can check the status on the portal.

## Documents you need

- A passport valid for at least 6 months on the day you apply
- A recent photo on a white background: JPEG, square, 10 KB to 1 MB, no glasses
- A scan of your passport's photo page in PDF
- A return or onward ticket and enough money for your stay

Every traveller, including children, needs their own passport and their own application. Your fingerprints and other biometric data are taken at immigration when you arrive in India.

## Where you can enter on an e-Visa

With an e-Visa you can enter India only through designated airports (Delhi is one of them) and seaports, not by land. You can leave through any immigration check post.

Before you travel, make sure your application status on the portal shows 'GRANTED', and carry a copy of the approval. Pay only on the official portal, indianvisaonline.gov.in.

## Travel to India with us

Our 9-day group tour of India covers Delhi and the cities of Rajasthan: Mandawa, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Udaipur and Pushkar. We fly from Tbilisi straight to Delhi, so the e-Visa works for this route. The tour page shows what is included.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for India?** Yes. Georgians can get an e-Visa on the official portal, indianvisaonline.gov.in.

**How much is the India tourist visa?** As of October 2026 the 30-day visa costs 25 USD from July to March and 10 USD from April to June; the 1-year visa is 40 USD and the 5-year visa 200 USD. A 3% bank charge is added.

**How early should I apply?** At least 4 days before arrival and no earlier than 120 days before.

**Can I get a visa at Delhi airport?** No. Visa on arrival is not available to Georgian citizens; get the e-Visa in advance.

**How long must my passport be valid?** At least 6 months on the day you apply.

**Does my child need a separate visa?** Yes, each traveller needs their own passport and their own application.

Sources:
- Indian e-Visa portal (Government of India): e-Visa types, eligible countries, instructions and FAQ: https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/tvoa.html
- Indian e-Visa portal: country-wise e-Tourist Visa fee (PDF): https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/images/Etourist_fee_final.pdf
- Indian e-Visa portal: country-wise e-Business / e-Medical visa fee (PDF): https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/images/eTV_revised_fee_final.pdf

# China Visa for Georgian Citizens: Visa-Free Rules and Hong Kong (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/china-visa-free-for-georgians/

No, Georgian citizens do not need a visa for a short trip to China. Since 28 May 2024 a mutual visa exemption agreement for ordinary passport holders has been in force: each stay must not exceed 30 days, and the total must not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. Hong Kong has its own rules: Georgians can stay there visa-free for up to 30 days (as of October 2026).

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for China?

Not for a short visit. On 10 April 2024 the governments of Georgia and China signed an agreement on mutual visa exemption for holders of ordinary passports. According to the official notice of the Chinese Embassy in Georgia, the agreement took effect at 00:00 Beijing time on 28 May 2024.

## The exact visa-free terms

According to the embassy notice, citizens of both countries holding a valid ordinary passport of their own country may enter, leave or transit the other country without a visa, provided that:

- each stay does not exceed 30 days
- the total stay does not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period

## When you still need a visa

The embassy notice also says you must apply for a visa before travel if you:

- plan to stay in China for more than 30 days
- are moving there to live
- plan to work, study, report as a journalist or do anything else that needs prior approval from the Chinese authorities

In those cases apply to the Chinese Embassy in Georgia.

The agreement covers ordinary passports only. Count your days: you cannot go over 30 days on one visit, and if you travel often, keep the 90-days-in-180 limit in mind.

## Hong Kong: separate rules

Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China with its own entry rules. The official table of the Hong Kong Immigration Department (updated August 2026) gives Georgian citizens a visa-free visit of 30 days.

The department's requirements for visitors:

- enough money to cover your stay
- a return or onward ticket (unless you are travelling on to mainland China or Macao)
- visitors may not work (paid or unpaid), set up or join a business, or study

If you want to stay in Hong Kong longer than 30 days, you must get a visa before you travel.

## Our China and Hong Kong tour

Our 13-day group tour starts in Beijing and continues to the Great Wall, Tianshui, Zhangjiajie, the Leshan Giant Buddha and Chengdu. We spend about 9 days in mainland China, then fly from Chengdu to Hong Kong for three days. Both stays fit within the visa-free limits.

For our tours your passport must be valid for at least 6 months. If you travel on another country's passport or on a service passport, check the rules with the embassy.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for China?** No, as long as each visit is no longer than 30 days and you stay no more than 90 days in total in any 180 days. This applies to ordinary passports.

**Since when is travel to China visa-free?** Since 00:00 Beijing time on 28 May 2024.

**When do I need a Chinese visa?** If you stay longer than 30 days, or go to live, work, study, report as a journalist or do anything else that needs prior approval.

**Do Georgians need a visa for Hong Kong?** No. According to the Hong Kong Immigration Department, Georgian citizens can visit visa-free for up to 30 days.

**Does your tour fit within the visa-free limits?** Yes. On our 13-day tour we spend about 9 days in mainland China and three days in Hong Kong.

Sources:
- Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Georgia: note on the China-Georgia agreement on mutual visa exemption for ordinary passport holders (27 May 2024): https://ge.china-embassy.gov.cn/lsfw/202405/t20240527_11312566.htm
- Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia: signing of the visa exemption agreement with China (10 April 2024): https://mfa.gov.ge/en/news/641804-saqartvelosa-da-chinets-mtavrobas-shoris-kheli-moetsera-ordinaluri-pasportebis-mphlobelta-savizo-mot
- Hong Kong Immigration Department: visit visa / entry permit requirements (updated August 2026): https://www.immd.gov.hk/eng/services/visas/visit-transit/visit-visa-entry-permit.html

# Sri Lanka and Maldives Visa for Georgian Citizens (2026)

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/sri-lanka-eta-visa-for-georgians/

Georgian citizens need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for Sri Lanka, obtained on eta.gov.lk before arrival: a 30-day tourist ETA costs 50 USD in advance, 60 USD on arrival, and is free for children under 12 (as of October 2026). The Maldives grants a tourist visa on arrival free of charge, but you must submit an online Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before you arrive.

## Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Sri Lanka?

Yes. For a short visit to Sri Lanka you need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), issued by the Department of Immigration and Emigration on the official site eta.gov.lk. The site says that all foreign nationals must obtain an ETA before arriving in Sri Lanka.

From 25 May 2026 citizens of 40 countries get the tourist ETA free of charge. Georgia is not on that list, so Georgians pay the ETA fee.

## How much is the Sri Lanka ETA for Georgians?

According to the official site, as of October 2026 the fees for 'all other countries' are:

- Tourist ETA obtained in advance (online, at a Sri Lankan mission or at the department's head office): 50 USD
- Tourist ETA on arrival: 60 USD
- Business ETA: 55 USD
- Transit up to 2 days: free
- Children under 12: tourist ETA free for up to 30 days

Online payment is by Visa, Mastercard or American Express only. The fee is not refunded.

Our Sri Lanka tour lists a visa fee of 60 USD as not included; that is the on-arrival price. An ETA obtained in advance costs 50 USD on the official site. On the Sri Lanka and Maldives tour the Sri Lanka visa fee is included. Please confirm the exact amount with our manager.

## What the ETA gives you and how long it lasts

- The tourist ETA is for 30 days with double entry: you can enter a second time within 30 days of your first arrival
- You must enter Sri Lanka within three months of the date the ETA is issued
- Your stay can be extended up to six months through the immigration department's online service after you arrive
- The tourist ETA does not cover work, journalism or NGO activities

## What the border officer will ask for

- A passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival
- A confirmed return ticket
- Enough money for your stay
- A copy of your ETA approval (the site advises carrying one)

## Maldives: tourist visa on arrival

According to the official Maldives Immigration website, the tourist visa is granted on arrival and no prior approval is needed. You must still meet the basic entry requirements:

- A passport with a machine-readable zone (MRZ), valid for at least one month
- A full itinerary: a confirmed return ticket and a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility
- Enough money for your stay
- A yellow fever vaccination certificate if you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever

Every foreigner must submit a Traveller Declaration on the IMUGA portal (imuga.immigration.gov.mv) within 96 hours before arriving in the Maldives. It is free. Each traveller, including children, needs their own declaration.

## Sri Lanka and the Maldives with us

In January 2027 we run two tours: a Sri Lanka tour with Sigiriya, Kandy, Ella, Mirissa and Colombo, and a tour that adds three nights in the Maldives. On the second tour the Sri Lanka visa fee and the Maldives electronic declaration are included. Each tour page shows what is included.

**Do Georgian citizens need a visa for Sri Lanka?** Yes, you need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), obtained on eta.gov.lk before you arrive.

**How much is the Sri Lanka ETA?** As of October 2026 a tourist ETA costs 50 USD in advance and 60 USD on arrival. It is free for children under 12.

**Is the ETA free for Georgians from 2026?** No. From 25 May 2026 the ETA is free for citizens of 40 countries, and Georgia is not one of them.

**How long can I stay in Sri Lanka?** The tourist ETA is for 30 days with double entry. It can be extended up to six months.

**Do Georgians need a visa for the Maldives?** A tourist visa is granted on arrival. Submit the Traveller Declaration on the IMUGA portal within 96 hours before arrival.

Sources:
- Sri Lanka ETA (Department of Immigration and Emigration): fees and the 40-country free ETA list from 25.05.2026: https://eta.gov.lk/slvisa/visainfo/fees.jsp?locale=en_US
- Sri Lanka ETA: how to apply and entry requirements: https://eta.gov.lk/slvisa/visainfo/apply.jsp?locale=en_US
- Sri Lanka ETA: short visit and types of ETA: https://eta.gov.lk/slvisa/visainfo/shortvisit.jsp?locale=en_US
- Sri Lanka ETA: FAQ: https://eta.gov.lk/slvisa/visainfo/faq.jsp?locale=en_US
- Maldives Immigration: Tourist Visa on arrival (updated 10/09/2026): https://www.immigration.gov.mv/visa/tourist-visa

# Kazbegi Day Trip from Tbilisi: Route, Drive and What to Wear

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/kazbegi-day-trip-from-tbilisi/

Our Kazbegi day tour leaves Tbilisi at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00. You see Dariali Monastery, the big and small Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. The longest walk is to the big waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty.

## What you see in one day

Our Kazbegi tour is a straightforward day trip up the Georgian Military Road. We leave Tbilisi in the morning and are back in the evening. The stops are:

- Dariali Monastery complex, in the Dariali gorge, which ends at the Russian border.
- The big Gveleti waterfall: a walk of 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty.
- The small Gveleti waterfall: an easy walk of about 500 m.
- Gergeti Trinity Church, below Mount Kazbek at about 2,170 m above sea level.
- The Gudauri panorama, a viewpoint on the way back.

Ananuri is not on our Kazbegi itinerary. If seeing it matters to you, ask us before you book.

## How long is the drive?

Stepantsminda, the town people call Kazbegi, is about 157 km north of Tbilisi and sits at around 1,740 m. The road crosses the Jvari Pass, its highest point at 2,379 m. Gudauri is about 120 km from Tbilisi at roughly 2,200 m.

The tour leaves at 07:00 and gets back around 22:00, so it is a full day with a lot of time in the vehicle. Get a good night's sleep and bring water and snacks for the road.

## How hard is the walking?

The longest walk on our tour is to the big Gveleti waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty, and the same distance back. The path to the small waterfall is easy, about 500 m. If the big waterfall is too much for you, you can visit only the small one.

You will feel the altitude more than you do in the city. If you have heart or breathing problems, ask your doctor before the trip and tell the tour escort.

## What to wear and bring, by season

Mountain weather changes fast and is cooler than Tbilisi. Dress in layers you can take off or put on easily.

- Summer: light clothes plus a warm top, a rain jacket, sunglasses, a hat and sunscreen.
- Spring and autumn: a warm jacket, a hat and waterproof shoes. Paths can be wet or muddy.
- Winter: a winter coat, gloves, a hat and shoes with non-slip soles. Gudauri is a ski resort whose season runs from December to April, so expect snow.
- Any season: comfortable walking or sports shoes, water, snacks and a power bank.
- For Gergeti Trinity Church: women need a headscarf and a skirt, men long trousers.

## Kazbegi or Truso?

The Kazbegi tour is about views and short walks. The Truso Gorge tour has much more walking: 6-7 km one way on an easy path, past colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Ketrisi village, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress. If you enjoy walking, choose Truso. If you want to see a lot without much effort, choose Kazbegi.

## What to do next

The tour page has the price and the latest details. Book a seat early, especially for weekends.

**What time does the Kazbegi tour leave and return?** It leaves at 07:00 and is back at about 22:00.

**Does the Kazbegi tour include Ananuri?** No. Our Kazbegi tour stops at Dariali, the Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama.

**How much walking is there?** The longest walk is to the big Gveleti waterfall: 1.2 km one way, medium difficulty. The small waterfall is an easy walk of about 500 m.

**How far is Kazbegi from Tbilisi?** Stepantsminda is about 157 km north of Tbilisi.

**What should I wear?** Dress in layers and bring a rain jacket and comfortable shoes. In winter, wear shoes with non-slip soles.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Stepantsminda (distance from Tbilisi, elevation): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepantsminda
- Wikipedia: Gergeti Trinity Church (elevation): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gergeti_Trinity_Church
- Wikipedia: Georgian Military Road (Jvari Pass, Darial Gorge): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_Military_Road
- Wikipedia: Gudauri (elevation, ski season): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudauri

# Best Day Trips from Tbilisi: Where to Go and Who Each Suits

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/best-day-trips-from-tbilisi/

For little walking, pick Kakheti, the colourful desert or Kazbegi. If you like hiking, pick Truso (6-7 km one way, easy) or Lagodekhi (8.3 km one way, medium). Go to the mountain routes in the warm months. Kakheti and the lowland routes work for most of the year.

## How to choose

Our day tours leave Tbilisi in the morning (06:00-08:00) and come back in the evening, by minibus with a tour escort. Two things matter most when choosing: how much walking you want and what time of year it is.

## Light walking: history and views

- Kakheti, Sighnaghi and Bodbe: Ninotsminda, Manavi Fortress, Bodbe Convent of St Nino and Sighnaghi. Good for families and older travellers.
- Classic Kakheti: Ujarma, Gombori Pass, Shuamta, Ikalto, Tetri Giorgi and Alaverdi.
- Other Kakheti routes: Nekresi, Ilia Lake, Gremi and Telavi, or Chailuri, Gurjaani Kvelatsminda, Zegaani and Sanagire.
- Kojori and Manglisi: close to the city, with fortresses and churches, ending at the Didgori battle memorial.
- Tianeti: Mamkoda, a bear shelter, Ertso fortress and Sioni Lake.
- Kvemo Kartli: Tserakvi, Gagi Fortress and the Tamarisi lakes.

The Kakheti, Kojori-Manglisi and Dzama tours run in any weather. They are postponed only if there is a problem with the road.

## Desert and easy walks

The colourful desert and David Gareja tour covers Dodo's Rka, the David Gareja monastery complex, the Mravaltskaro colourful mountains and reservoir. Walking is easy, about 1 km in total. If you only want to see the cave monasteries, there is also a Sabereebi tour.

There is little shade in the desert. On warm days bring water, a hat and sunscreen.

## Mountains and waterfalls

- Kazbegi: Dariali, the Gveleti waterfalls, Gergeti Trinity Church and the Gudauri panorama. 1.2 km one way to the big waterfall (medium) and 500 m to the small one (easy). Stepantsminda is about 157 km from Tbilisi.
- Khada Gorge: the confluence of the White and Black Aragvi and the Tskere and Rostiani waterfalls. A 4.2 km walk one way, easy.
- Truso Gorge: colourful travertines, the 'bottomless' lake, Abano Convent and Zakagori Fortress. 6-7 km one way, easy but long.
- Lagodekhi: up the Ninoskhevi gorge to the Gurgeniani waterfall. 8.3 km one way, medium and hard in places. This is the longest trail among our day tours.

## Lakes and the high plateau

- Javakheti lakes: Paravani (Georgia's largest lake), the Poka monastery and convent, Saghamo Lake, Gorelovka and the Madatapa reserve.
- Tabatskuri: over the Tskhratskaro Pass (2,462 m) to Tabatskuri village (2,000 m), with free time at the lake and Timotesubani Monastery. This one leaves at 06:00.
- Samtskhe-Javakheti: Zarzma, Chule, Akhaltsikhe's Rabati and Sapara, with guide Giorgi Beridze-Berjavakhi.

## Which season?

On the high mountain routes (Kazbegi, Truso, Tabatskuri, Javakheti), weather and road conditions decide a lot. Winter there means snow and frost, so plan these for the warm months. Gudauri's ski season, for example, runs from December to April. Kakheti, Gareja, Kojori and Kvemo Kartli are easy to visit at different times of year. The desert gets hot in summer, so spring and autumn are more comfortable there.

Exact dates and prices are on each tour page. If you have a health condition, ask us how much walking a tour involves before you book.

## What to do next

Pick one or two routes, check the tour page and book a seat. If you can't decide, write to us and tell us how much you can walk and who you are travelling with.

**Which day trip is the easiest?** The Kakheti routes, Kojori-Manglisi and the colourful desert, where walking is about 1 km in total and easy.

**Which one is for hikers?** Truso (6-7 km one way, easy) and Lagodekhi (8.3 km one way, medium and hard in places).

**What time do the tours leave?** Most leave at 07:00 or 08:00. Tabatskuri leaves at 06:00. The exact time is on each tour page.

**Can I go to Kazbegi or Truso in winter?** The mountains get snow in winter and road conditions change. Plan mountain routes for the warm months and check winter dates with us.

**Where should I go with children?** The easiest options are the Kakheti routes, Kojori-Manglisi, Tianeti and the colourful desert.

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Stepantsminda (distance from Tbilisi): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepantsminda
- Wikipedia: Gudauri (ski season): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudauri

# Cappadocia: Best Time to Visit and Hot-Air Balloon Flights

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/cappadocia-hot-air-balloons-best-time/

According to GoTürkiye, Türkiye's official tourism portal, the best time for a balloon ride is spring or autumn, when the weather is milder and more settled. Flights start just before sunrise, depend on the weather and can be cancelled. On our tour the flight is optional and costs 200-250 EUR.

## When to go to Cappadocia

GoTürkiye says balloon rides run all year, but the best time is spring or autumn, when the weather is generally milder and more regular than at other times. Its autumn feature names September and October as the best months to enjoy the landscape, when average temperatures drop to milder levels.

Cappadocia lies southeast of Ankara and is best known for its geology, above all the fairy chimneys. The Göreme Open-Air Museum has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1985.

## How a balloon flight works

According to GoTürkiye, flights start just before sunrise. Guests start getting ready around 4:00 am, and a bus collects them from the hotel shortly after.

Everything depends on the weather. Türkiye's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (SHGM) has a separate circular on meteorological evaluation for balloon flights in Cappadocia. In practice, if it is windy or the weather is bad, flights can be delayed or cancelled that same morning.

A balloon flight is never guaranteed. If it doesn't happen, our programme also has time for photos with the balloons in the background. Ask about cancellation and refund terms when you book.

## What a flight costs on our tour

On our 6-day bus tour to Cappadocia, Amasya and Ordu, the balloon flight is optional at 200-250 EUR and is not included in the tour price. On the morning of day 3 you either fly or take photos of the balloons from the ground. The day continues with the Göreme Open-Air Museum, Tokali Church, Uchisar Castle and Pigeon Valley.

## What to wear

- Flights take off at dawn, and mornings are cool, especially in spring and autumn. Wear layers and bring a warm jacket.
- Comfortable closed shoes. Getting in and out of the basket can be awkward.
- A hat, against the sun and the heat from the burner.
- For walking in the valleys: trainers, water and sunglasses.
- For churches and monasteries: covered shoulders.

## Tips

- Book your flight early, with help from the tour escort.
- If you have a health condition, ask your doctor before flying.
- Don't take a cancellation personally: flights are cancelled for safety. The balloons look beautiful from the ground too.

## What to do next

Check dates and price on the tour page. When you book, tell us if you want a balloon flight so we can plan ahead.

**When is the best time for a balloon ride in Cappadocia?** GoTürkiye says spring or autumn. For autumn it singles out September and October.

**Can the flight be cancelled?** Yes. Flights depend on the weather and can be cancelled that same morning if it is windy or the weather is bad.

**How much is the balloon flight on your tour?** It is optional and costs 200-250 EUR. It is not included in the tour price.

**What time does the flight start?** Just before sunrise. Preparation starts at about 4:00 am.

**What should I wear?** Warm layers, a jacket, closed shoes and a hat.

# Keukenhof 2027: When the Tulip Park in the Netherlands Is Open

URL: https://besttraveler.ge/en/blog/keukenhof-tulip-season/

According to the official site keukenhof.nl, Keukenhof is open from Thursday 18 March to Sunday 9 May 2027, daily from 8:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 18:15. Flowering depends on the weather, so nobody can say in advance exactly which week will be best.

## When is Keukenhof open in 2027?

The official Keukenhof website says the park is open from 18 March to 9 May 2027, every day including Sundays and public holidays, from 8:00 to 19:00. Entry closes at 18:15. The address is Stationsweg 166a, Lisse.

The flower season covers these spring weeks, so your travel dates need to fall inside that window.

## When do the tulips bloom?

Keukenhof says the flowering season follows the rhythm of nature and depends on the weather, which makes it hard to name the best time to visit. Early in the season you see early bloomers such as crocuses, daffodils, hyacinths and early tulips. Later, the later varieties come out, including larger tulips. The website also has a bloom report showing current conditions.

## Tickets

- According to the official FAQ, 2027 starting prices for adults are 21 EUR online and 27 EUR at the box office. Children aged 4-17 start at 11 EUR online, and under-4s go free.
- A ticket is valid only for the time slot you book, with no earlier or later entry.
- The site recommends buying online: it is cheaper and guarantees your preferred date and time.
- Visitors spend about 3 hours in the park on average.

If you are on one of our tours, you don't need to arrange a ticket yourself. Keukenhof is in the programme, and the entry price is shown on the tour page.

## How to plan

- Pick dates between 18 March and 9 May. Early and late in the season you see different flowers.
- According to the official site, the park is quieter before 10:30 and after 16:00. Morning and evening light is better for photos.
- Dress in layers and bring an umbrella or rain jacket, because spring weather changes fast.
- Wear comfortable shoes, since you will walk a lot.

## Our tulip tours

We run two 8-day group tours that include Keukenhof:

- Belgium and the Netherlands: flight from Kutaisi. Brussels, Amsterdam, Giethoorn, Volendam, Zaandam, Keukenhof, The Hague, Ghent and Bruges.
- Netherlands and Germany: flight from Tbilisi to Düsseldorf. Castles, Paleis Het Loo, Giethoorn, Zaanse Schans, Amsterdam, Keukenhof and Utrecht.

Spring dates and prices are on the tour pages. If dates aren't listed yet, write to us and we'll hold a place for you.

**When is Keukenhof open in 2027?** According to the official site, from 18 March to 9 May 2027, daily from 8:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 18:15.

**When is the best time to see tulips?** Keukenhof says flowering depends on the weather. Crocuses, daffodils and early tulips come first, and the larger tulips later.

**How much is a ticket?** The official FAQ gives 2027 starting prices of 21 EUR online and 27 EUR at the box office for adults, and from 11 EUR online for children aged 4-17.

**Where do I buy tickets?** On the official site, keukenhof.nl. The ticket is valid only for your time slot.

**Which of your tours include Keukenhof?** The Belgium-Netherlands tour (from Kutaisi) and the Netherlands-Germany tour (from Tbilisi).

Sources:
